methodologyMarkdown:
## Overview
OHCHR's legacy document database at https://ap.ohchr.org/documents/mainec.aspx is a server-rendered ASP.NET WebForms application. It exposes a categorized search interface over human-rights body documents (Concluding Observations, reports, etc.).

## Search
The landing page renders ONLY a search form: Body, Session and Type dropdowns plus refine filters for Country, Subject, Mandate and Symbol Number, with All-Words/Any toggles. A ?syb={query} parameter is referenced by the interface, but on a plain GET the page returns the empty form with NO document or PDF links. Because it is WebForms, actual results require a POST carrying __VIEWSTATE / __EVENTVALIDATION / __doPostBack state, not a stateless GET.

## Filters
Body, Session, Type, Country, Subject, Mandate, Symbol Number - all driven through the post-back form rather than clean URL parameters.

## Download
Document PDFs are only reachable from the results grid produced after form submission (record-page flow). No direct-PDF links exist on the initial page.

## Metadata & Enrichment
No REST/JSON API. Metadata (symbol, body, session, type) appears in the results grid. Enrichment mode is none.

## Limitations
HONEST ASSESSMENT: this is a stateful WebForms app. A stateless scraper cannot retrieve documents from a plain GET; it must either replay the __VIEWSTATE post-back sequence or drive the form with a headless browser. Only browseAll is claimed as a near-stub; search/download over a simple URL are NOT verified.
probeNotes: WebFetch of https://ap.ohchr.org/documents/mainec.aspx returned a server-rendered ASP.NET page containing only the search form (Body/Session/Type + Country/Subject/Mandate/Symbol filters, All-Words/Any toggles) and NO document or PDF links. Results depend on a WebForms post-back, so plain-GET scraping yields no documents. No API.
